L0.MANAGE.label: MANAGE
L0.MANAGE.definition: Control, Value & Optimize Data Assets. The DOM's operational core and largest macro-process (5 L2, 26 L3). Controls data assets through their lifecycle, measures economic value, ensures security and compliance, and provides portfolio management driving BUILD and RUN priorities.

L0.BUILD.label: BUILD
L0.BUILD.definition: Construct Platforms & Data Flows. Constructs the technical platforms and data flows that MANAGE controls and RUN delivers through. 60-70% of capacity is demand-driven by MANAGE Portfolio Management; 30-40% addresses technical debt, platform evolution, and innovation.

L0.GOVERN.label: GOVERN
L0.GOVERN.definition: Set Direction, Rules & Architecture. Establishes the strategic compass, governance framework, and architectural standards guiding all data activities. Answers: Why invest in data? What rules apply? How should the data landscape be structured?

L0.RUN.label: RUN
L0.RUN.definition: Deliver Value to the Business. The value realization engine. Translates everything GOVERN directs, MANAGE controls, and BUILD constructs into consumable business outcomes. Where data management proves its worth — or fails to.

GOVERN.L2.1.label: Data Strategy & Direction
GOVERN.L2.1.definition: Defines and steers the enterprise data strategy, investment framework, and organizational design. Provides the strategic compass guiding all GOVERN, MANAGE, BUILD, and RUN activities. Ensures data capabilities serve business objectives with measurable returns.

l3s.label: Data Strategy & Communication
l3s.definition: Strategic alignment and stakeholder buy-in for data initiatives.

l3s.label: Data Valuation & Investment Framework
l3s.definition: Economic justification and portfolio logic for data investments.

l3s.label: Organizational Design & Operating Model
l3s.definition: Centralized vs. federated operating model decisions for data capabilities.

GOVERN.L2.2.label: Data Governance & Oversight
GOVERN.L2.2.definition: Establishes and operates the governance framework: policies, decision rights, accountability structures, compliance programs, stewardship models, and AI governance. Translates strategic direction (L2.1) into enforceable rules and oversight mechanisms.

l3s.label: Governance Framework & Decision Rights
l3s.definition: Policy architecture and enforcement mechanisms for data governance.

l3s.label: Data Compliance, Legal & Privacy
l3s.definition: Compliance with GDPR, DORA, AI Act and other regulatory frameworks.

l3s.label: Ownership & Stewardship
l3s.definition: Accountability structures and domain responsibility for data assets.

l3s.label: Data Audit & Certification
l3s.definition: Verification and attestation of data management practices and compliance.

l3s.label: ML/AI Model Governance
l3s.definition: Ethical AI governance, model lifecycle management and AI Act compliance.

GOVERN.L2.3.label: Data Architecture & Standards
GOVERN.L2.3.definition: Establishes the enterprise data architecture, architectural principles, security-by-design foundations, and technology standards. Provides the technical governance blueprint that BUILD constructs, MANAGE operates within, and RUN delivers through.

l3s.label: Enterprise Information Architecture
l3s.definition: Data landscape blueprint defining the enterprise information structure.

l3s.label: Architecture Principles & Security-by-Design
l3s.definition: Non-negotiable architectural standards and security-by-design foundations.

l3s.label: Technology Radar & Reference Architecture
l3s.definition: Technology lifecycle management preventing premature adoption and dangerous tech debt.

MANAGE.L2.1.label: Data Economics & Performance
MANAGE.L2.1.definition: Establishes the economic framework for treating data as a measurable business asset through systematic valuation, cost accounting, monetization, and portfolio management. Transforms data management from a cost center into a value-demonstrating discipline.

l3s.label: Data Asset Valuation
l3s.definition: Systematic measurement of data asset worth using economic methodologies.

l3s.label: Cost Accounting & Chargeback
l3s.definition: True cost allocation for data capabilities across the organization.

l3s.label: Portfolio Management & Demand Prioritization
l3s.definition: Investment allocation channeling 60-70% of BUILD capacity through economically rationalized priorities.

l3s.label: Data Monetization & Value Realization
l3s.definition: Mechanisms for capturing and demonstrating value from data assets.

l3s.label: Economic Performance Reporting
l3s.definition: CFO-grade ROI measurement and reporting for data investments.

MANAGE.L2.2.label: Data Security, Privacy & Compliance
MANAGE.L2.2.definition: Implements comprehensive data security, privacy, and compliance protecting assets through access control, classification, encryption, breach detection, consent management, and regulatory engagement. Ensures confidentiality, integrity, and availability while enabling appropriate and lawful data usage.

l3s.label: Role-Based Data Access
l3s.definition: Access control determining who accesses what data under which conditions.

l3s.label: Data Classification, Protection & Encryption
l3s.definition: Data-centric protection through classification schemes and encryption.

l3s.label: Data Breach Detection & Incident Response
l3s.definition: Threat detection, incident response and breach management.

l3s.label: GDPR Consent & Preference Management
l3s.definition: Granular, traceable management of consent as a data asset — atomic capability concept.

l3s.label: Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA)
l3s.definition: Risk assessment for data processing activities under GDPR and DORA.

l3s.label: Regulatory Affairs & Authority Management
l3s.definition: Interface management with regulatory authorities and compliance bodies.

MANAGE.L2.3.label: Knowledge & Metadata Management
MANAGE.L2.3.definition: Manages the enterprise knowledge layer: data standards, semantic models, metadata, business glossary, data lineage, and catalogue operations. Enables data discovery, shared understanding, and confident usage across the organization.

l3s.label: Data Standards Management
l3s.definition: Naming conventions, formatting rules and data standards governance.

l3s.label: Data Modelling
l3s.definition: Conceptual, logical and physical data modelling across the enterprise.

l3s.label: Metadata & Business Glossary
l3s.definition: Shared business vocabulary and metadata management.

l3s.label: Data Lineage & Impact Analysis
l3s.definition: End-to-end traceability of data flows, critical for AI Act compliance.

l3s.label: Semantic Models & Taxonomy Management
l3s.definition: Meaning structures, taxonomies and semantic layer management.

l3s.label: Data Dictionaries & Catalogue Operations
l3s.definition: Discovery platform operations and data dictionary management.

MANAGE.L2.4.label: Data Asset Management
MANAGE.L2.4.definition: Manages data assets through their complete lifecycle: master data, reference data, quality, anonymization, and retention. Ensures assets remain accurate, consistent, secure, and compliant from creation to deletion.

l3s.label: Master & Reference Data Management
l3s.definition: Golden records, master data management and reference data governance.

l3s.label: Data Quality Management
l3s.definition: Fitness for purpose — appears as Indispensable in 10 of 12 frameworks mapped.

l3s.label: Data Anonymization & Pseudonymization
l3s.definition: Privacy-preserving techniques for data protection and AI training data.

l3s.label: Data Retention, Archival & Deletion
l3s.definition: Lifecycle compliance from creation to deletion.

l3s.label: Test Data Management
l3s.definition: Non-production data management for development and testing.

MANAGE.L2.5.label: Data Operations & Reliability
MANAGE.L2.5.definition: Ensures data capabilities deliver agreed performance, availability, and quality through SLA definition, operational monitoring, business continuity, and continuous improvement. Brings operational discipline and reliability engineering to the data function.

l3s.label: Service Level Agreement Definition & Monitoring
l3s.definition: SLA architecture for data services.

l3s.label: Business Continuity & Disaster Recovery
l3s.definition: Resilience planning and disaster recovery for data services.

l3s.label: Service Performance Reporting
l3s.definition: Delivery measurement and performance reporting for data services.

l3s.label: Continuous Service Improvement
l3s.definition: Maturity progression closing the loop: RUN performance feeds back into improvement cycles.

BUILD.L2.1.label: Data Integration & Ingestion
BUILD.L2.1.definition: Establishes and manages data integration and ingestion across the enterprise through pipeline orchestration, real-time streaming, batch processing, change data capture, and external data acquisition. The connective tissue between data sources and consumption platforms.

l3s.label: Data Orchestration & Choreography
l3s.definition: Pipeline coordination and workflow orchestration for data movement.

l3s.label: Real-Time Data Acquisition
l3s.definition: Streaming ingestion and real-time data capture.

l3s.label: Batch Data Transfer & Processing
l3s.definition: Scheduled data movement and batch processing pipelines.

l3s.label: Change Data Capture & Event Sourcing
l3s.definition: Incremental capture of data changes and event-based data sourcing.

l3s.label: External Data Supplier Management
l3s.definition: Third-party data feeds and external supplier integration.

l3s.label: Screen & Web Scraping
l3s.definition: Unstructured data acquisition from screens and web sources.

BUILD.L2.2.label: Data Platform & Storage
BUILD.L2.2.definition: Establishes and operates the data platform and storage landscape making data available for operational, analytical, and exploratory consumption. Covers transactional systems, analytical stores, data lakes, and virtualization — the infrastructure layer on which all data capabilities depend.

l3s.label: Transactional Data Platforms
l3s.definition: OLTP systems and transactional data platform management.

l3s.label: Data Lake Management
l3s.definition: Raw and staged data storage in data lake architectures.

l3s.label: Data Warehouse & Data Mart Management
l3s.definition: Analytical serving layer through data warehouses and data marts.

l3s.label: Data Virtualization & Federation
l3s.definition: Logical access layer providing virtual views without physical data movement.

BUILD.L2.3.label: AI & Data Engineering
BUILD.L2.3.definition: Constructs the engineering infrastructure enabling AI and machine learning capabilities: feature management, ML pipelines, model registries, and inference serving. Bridges data platform capabilities and AI-powered applications in RUN.

l3s.label: Feature Store & Training Data Management
l3s.definition: Centralised management of ML features ensuring consistency between training and serving, and governance of training datasets including versioning and lineage.

l3s.label: ML Pipeline & Model Infrastructure
l3s.definition: Engineering and orchestration of end-to-end ML pipelines covering data preparation, training runs, evaluation, and automated retraining in production environments.

l3s.label: LLM Serving & Inference Infrastructure
l3s.definition: Infrastructure for deploying and serving large language models and AI inference workloads at scale, covering latency management, cost control, and model hosting patterns.

l3s.label: Model Registry & Versioning
l3s.definition: Centralised catalogue and lifecycle management for all ML and AI models: versioning, lineage, performance tracking, promotion gates, and deprecation across environments.

RUN.L2.1.label: Data Product Delivery
RUN.L2.1.definition: Delivers consumable data products through business intelligence, self-service analytics, forecasting, APIs, and KPI delivery. Ensures data products are discoverable and accessible. The primary value realization mechanism for most organizations.

l3s.label: Business Intelligence & Reporting Delivery
l3s.definition: Structured reports, visualizations, and dashboards delivering business intelligence to decision-makers across the organization.

l3s.label: Self-Service Analytics
l3s.definition: Empowers business users to explore, query, and analyse data autonomously through governed self-service platforms and semantic layers.

l3s.label: Data Product Catalogue & Discoverability
l3s.definition: Makes data products findable, understandable, and trustworthy through cataloguing, ownership declaration, SLA exposure, and consumer-facing discovery interfaces.

l3s.label: Forecasting & Simulation Analytics
l3s.definition: Predictive data products through forecasting and simulation.

l3s.label: Data API & Services Management
l3s.definition: Programmatic data access through APIs — critical for Data Mesh implementations.

l3s.label: KPI & Metrics Delivery
l3s.definition: Business measurement through KPI and metrics delivery.

RUN.L2.2.label: Data Insights
RUN.L2.2.definition: Generates advanced insights and intelligent capabilities through data science, machine learning, and AI applications. Encompasses predictive analytics, NLP, generative AI, enterprise search, ML experimentation, and decision intelligence.

l3s.label: Advanced Analytics & Data Science
l3s.definition: Statistical modeling, machine learning and advanced analytical capabilities.

l3s.label: NLP & Conversational AI
l3s.definition: Natural language processing and conversational AI applications.

l3s.label: Generative AI & LLM Applications
l3s.definition: Design and operation of generative AI applications leveraging large language models, including prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation, and enterprise LLM deployment.

l3s.label: Enterprise Search & Information Retrieval
l3s.definition: Knowledge discovery through enterprise search and information retrieval.

l3s.label: ML Model Development & Experimentation
l3s.definition: End-to-end machine learning model development lifecycle: problem framing, feature engineering, training, evaluation, and experiment tracking prior to production deployment.

l3s.label: Decision Intelligence & Optimization
l3s.definition: Automated and augmented decision-making through optimization models, simulation, prescriptive analytics, and decision support systems embedded in business processes.

RUN.L2.3.label: DataOps & Platform Operations
RUN.L2.3.definition: Ensures continuous, reliable, and cost-efficient operation of data pipelines, platforms, and data products in production. Encompasses monitoring, incident management, capacity planning, DataOps practices, and FinOps for data infrastructure. The operational backbone that sustains the value delivered by RUN.L2.1 and RUN.L2.2.

l3s.label: Data Pipeline Operations & Monitoring
l3s.definition: Day-to-day operation and monitoring of data ingestion, transformation, and delivery pipelines. Includes scheduling, failure detection, alerting, restart management, and DataOps automation practices (CI/CD for data). Ensures pipelines run reliably within agreed SLAs.

l3s.label: Data Platform Observability
l3s.definition: End-to-end visibility into the health, freshness, volume, schema, and distribution of data across the platform. Encompasses data quality monitoring in production (data observability tools such as Monte Carlo, Bigeye, or Soda), lineage-based impact analysis for anomalies, and automated data freshness alerting. Distinct from BUILD-time testing.

l3s.label: Data Incident Management
l3s.definition: Structured response to data incidents in production: pipeline failures, data quality breaches, latency violations, and data loss events. Covers triage, escalation, root-cause analysis, remediation, post-mortem, and prevention. Aligns with ITIL incident management practices adapted for data-intensive systems and integrates with MANAGE_L2.2 for security incidents.

l3s.label: Data Infrastructure Capacity Planning
l3s.definition: Forward-looking management of compute, storage, and network capacity for data workloads. Includes demand forecasting, resource reservation, auto-scaling policies, tier management (hot/warm/cold storage), and infrastructure lifecycle decisions. Prevents capacity-induced outages while avoiding over-provisioning and associated FinOps waste.

l3s.label: Data Product Lifecycle Operations
l3s.definition: End-to-end operational management of data products through their lifecycle: launch, version management, deprecation, and decommissioning. Includes managing data product SLAs, consumer notification, backward compatibility, and the DataContract enforcement between producers and consumers. Operationalises the Data Mesh product ownership principle in production.

l3s.label: Data FinOps & Cloud Cost Management
l3s.definition: Continuous monitoring, allocation, and optimisation of cloud and on-premises data infrastructure costs. Covers per-workload cost attribution (chargeback to BU or data product), query cost optimization (BigQuery slot management, Redshift concurrency), storage tier management, LLM inference cost governance, and unit-economics dashboards for data products. The operational complement to MANAGE_L2.1 economic governance.

The operational complement to MANAGE_L2.1 economic governance.
